paper_metadata.title: Selective laser melting additive manufacturing of tungsten with niobium alloying: Microstructure and suppression mechanism of microcracks

evidence.quote: Microcrack suppression is a challenging issue in additive manufacturing of tungsten heavy alloys (WHAs) due to the high melting point and brittleness of tungsten (W). In this study, W-5Nb samples with a high density and few defects were successfully manufactured by introducing niobium (Nb) using selective laser melting (SLM) technique

Solid solution strengthening occurred in W with Nb alloying and also contributed to improvement of grain bonding strength.

Inclined microcracks were generally caused by residual stresses in the overlap region between the scan tracks and propagate with the synergistic effect of residual stresses at both parallel and perpendicular directions with the scan tracks.
However, perpendicular microcracks run through single or even multiple fusion tracks and were mainly induced by excessive thermal gradient stresses along the scan trace direction.
Due to high laser power, excessive convection and sputtering behavior of the melt pool would result in the introduction of gas to form pores.
The distribution segregation extent and density of nanopores formed by WxOy gasification were reduced, which was beneficial for improvement of grain bonding strength.
Another suppression mechanism of microcracks is the strong solid solution strengthening effect generated by Nb alloying.
